project: What If You Could Control Probability?
tone: cinematic minimalist SVG 2D/2.5D, dark consequences, one power setting at a time

cast.protagonist: ReferenceHero coral hoodie, black round head, white minimal face

worldCamera: Treat each scene as one fixed SVG world. Camera pans/zooms the ENTIRE scene as a single parent transform. Do NOT animate scenery independently simply to simulate a camera.
powerRule: Only one event's probability can be set. Setting a different target immediately removes the old guarantee.
ending: Freeze BEFORE truck collision; no injury impact shown.

audio.voice: Candidate Piper en_US-joe-medium TTS staged at studio/public/probability-longform/voice.mp3; 230-second rough timeline-aligned MP3
audio.timing: All 27 measured segments fit their assigned scene windows; editorial beats documented in EDITING_MAP.json
audio.sfx: Original 230-second procedural Foley, synchronized to real coin contacts, lottery digit locks, action beats
audio.music: Original 230-second synthesized suspense score reused from prior sound-design branch
audio.mix: A single 230-second loudness-balanced master.mp3 is used for video render. Editable voice.mp3, sfx.mp3 and music.mp3 remain present separately; narrator voice remains unapproved.
audio.visualFixes: Hand-to-table coin flight and settle; 10 actual flips; winning lottery ticket unchanged across cut; debris delayed until fractures
audio.master: studio/public/probability-longform/master.mp3 — phone-friendly limited audio, no doubled effects

render.notes: User explicitly requested no further renders; do not trigger Remotion render or GitHub Actions video workflow.

shots.voice: A few hours earlier, he had discovered the strangest ability imaginable.

shots.voice: Then he tried a lottery ticket. Not because he needed the money. Because he wanted to know if there was a limit.

shots.voice: The numbers matched. Every single one.

shots.voice: It felt like he had found a cheat code for real life. But he missed the tiny warning on the screen.

shots.voice: He decided there was one setting more valuable than money: the chance of dying. Zero percent.

shots.voice: He could change it to one hundred. But he'd have to overwrite the protection keeping him alive.

shots.voice: He stared at the choice. Stay buried and guaranteed alive? Or escape, with no guarantee of what happens next?

shots.voice: His escape was guaranteed. His survival wasn't. Controlling one probability doesn't mean controlling what happens next.
